name: Uterine Leiomyomas (FIGO Staging, Medical Therapy, Myomectomy) and Adenomyosis

reference.source: Gynaecology by Ten Teachers 21st Edition / FIGO Classification of Leiomyomas
clinicalPearls: Uterine leiomyomas are monoclonal benign smooth muscle tumors dependent on estrogen and progesterone
FIGO classifies fibroids into Types 0 to 8 based on submucosal, intramural, and subserosal anatomical location
Submucosal fibroids (FIGO Types 0, 1, 2) cause severe menorrhagia and subfertility, resectable via hysteroscopy
GnRH agonists induce reversible hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, reducing fibroid volume by thirty to fifty percent preoperatively
Adenomyosis features ectopic endometrial glands in myometrium, diagnosed by junctional zone thickness exceeding twelve millimeters on MRI
reference.pathophysiology: Leiomyomas originate from somatic mutations (e.g., MED12 mutations) in individual myometrial stem cells, stimulated by local estrogen and progesterone receptor overexpression. Excess extracellular matrix deposition creates pseudocapsules. In adenomyosis, mechanical invagination of the endometrial basalis into myometrial stroma triggers smooth muscle hyperplasia and impaired junctional zone contractility, causing menorrhagia and severe dysmenorrhea.
additionalDifferentials: Leiomyosarcoma (rapid postmenopausal growth, solitary heterogenous mass)
additionalInvestigations: Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (gold standard for junctional zone thickness)
Saline infusion sonohysterography or diagnostic hysteroscopy for cavity involvement
